messages:
sylvia: Heads up — we hit a recurring p95 spike (~180-300ms) between gpu-node-13 and gpu-node-21 during the 09:30-10:30 batch ramp window this morning. Impacting small-batch jobs and preempting tail-latency SLOs. Anyone seen this pattern?
raj: Yep saw traces. Correlates with increased short-lived connections from the new dynamic-batcher. Starts ~09:28, peaks at 09:35, and tapers by 09:50. No packet loss reported at app layer but the TCP retransmit count climbs.
mike: grabbed kernel counters on gpu-node-21: ixgbe stats show tx_errors and tx_failed in bursts. Also NIC queues show heavy backpressure.
alexa: I ran a quick ethtool dump on both ends:
```
# on gpu-node-13
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "tx_|rx_"
tx_packets: 15432123
tx_errors: 42
tx_dropped: 512
rx_packets: 15299811
rx_errors: 0
rx_dropped: 8
```
and on gpu-node-21:
```
rx_packets: 15432345
rx_errors: 0
rx_dropped: 490
tx_packets: 15431001
tx_errors: 0
tx_dropped: 2
```
alexa: tx_dropped on node-13 aligns with retransmit spikes. Could be MTU/path MTU blackhole or driver coalescing under burst.
sylvia: I also collected an ibv_rc_pingpong run (RDMA path) — latency doesn't spike as much, but connection resets increase: 6 resets during the window.
raj: pushing a tcpdump during the ramp shows bursts of duplicate ACKs and many small packets ~1440B, so maybe PMTU or fragmentation.
mike: are we doing any offload toggles? TSO/GSO/LRO on? If offloading flips under load it can cause more packets.
alexa: current settings (on both): TSO:on GSO:on GRO:on rx-checksumming:on tx-checksumming:on
sylvia: can we try disabling GRO on node-13 in canary to see if p95 improves? small config change, quick rollback.
raj: +1. Also suggest moving the batcher pool to use fewer long-lived connections (increase request coalescing) to reduce bursts.
infra-bot: deploy-trigger: smoke-canary/gro-disable/node-13 queued by raj at 1712345690
mike: changed GRO=off on node-13 at 09:34:10 — monitoring.
alexa: immediate effect: p95 dropped from ~220ms to ~85ms within 45s. Retransmit counters stopped growing.
sylvia: good signal. Can we replicate on node-21?
raj: let's do a rolling canary: node-21 next, then small shard. Also file an incident ticket to track root cause — driver/firmware? MTU mismatch? overlay?
mike: opening ticket INF-2026 with logs, ethtool output, tcpdump, and ib verbs capture.
sylvia: long-term: engineering to test interaction between dynamic-batcher connection churn and NIC offload heuristics. For now, keep GRO off on batcher pool nodes during peak windows and monitor cost/CPU tradeoff.
raj: note: CPU on nodes increased ~6% after GRO off, but latency SLOs are back.
alexa: adding short playbook to eng-infra runbook: if p95>150ms during batch window, disable GRO on affected nodes, collect dumps, escalate to infra if persists.
sylvia: thanks team. Follow-up: firmware update scheduled for this rack Thursday — include NIC driver tests there.
raj: thanks, closing thread once INF-2026 created and playbook merged.
